problem: End-to-end DRL PointGoal navigation agents need hundreds of millions of interaction steps and lack semantic reasoning; occupancy-map-based agents ignore semantic cues, and a naive CNN on a semantic map fails to exploit the richer information.
motivation: Humans use semantic landmarks and spatial structure to navigate efficiently. Agents should reach good performance under a limited training budget (14M steps vs 75M+), which requires a richer scene representation and a way to extract relevant parts of it.
key_idea: Build a top-down egocentric bag-of-classes semantic map from depth and semantic segmentation, and read it with a 2-D map Transformer that uses Gaussian-kernel-based positional embeddings centered on the agent, trained with PPO plus an exploration reward.
insight: A semantic map alone gives no benefit without attention: RGBD+SEM has SPL 41 but success falls to 49 (vs 51 for RGBD), while adding the Transformer gives SPL 47 and success 54. The Transformer on an occupancy map gives little gain (SPL 44), so attention pays off only when the map content is rich. Exploration reward alone lifts SPL from 34 to 38.
method: Egocentric semantic map: back-project depth to a point cloud, transform it with the agent pose, project it top-down, crop to radius r and rotate so heading is up; each cell stores a binary bag-of-classes vector over N_c classes.
Visual encoder f_CNN: a 3-layer CNN (Habitat-style) over concatenated RGB and depth giving r_emb.
Egocentric map Transformer f_MAP: a 2-layer BERT-style model with 4 heads and 128-d embeddings, using 1x1 convolutions to preserve spatial layout, then pooling over both spatial dimensions.

Gaussian positional indices: a 2r x 2r Gaussian kernel (scale r/2) centered on the agent; each unique value gets an integer index into learned positional embeddings, giving finer resolution near the agent.
Policy head: concatenate the visual and map features, fuse them with an FC layer, and feed the result with the previous action into a 1-layer GRU, followed by actor and critic heads.

Rewards and optimization: PPO with a goal-distance-change reward, a success bonus, a time penalty, a collision penalty of 0.01λ, and an auxiliary exploration reward equal to the fraction of map tiles revealed.

setting.backbone: 3-layer CNN + 2-layer map Transformer (BERT-style) + GRU policy, trained from scratch with PPO
setting.training_data: RL in Habitat on Matterport3D train scenes, 14M steps of experience (7.7M for the predicted-semantics variant)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB + depth + semantic segmentation (GT from simulator; Mask R-CNN in one variant) + GPS/compass
setting.action_space: low-level discrete Habitat actions (move forward, turn, stop)
setting.privileged: GT depth, GT semantic labels and GT pose (GPS+compass) used for the main results; a Mask R-CNN predicted-semantics variant is also reported

results: Under a 14M-step budget MaAST reaches SPL 47 and success 54 on Matterport3D val. This beats RGBD PPO (34/51), RGBD+occupancy map (43/52) and the SLAM baseline (SPL 42). The gain is mainly in path efficiency rather than success rate.
limitations: Main results rely on ground-truth depth, semantics and pose; the predicted-semantics variant was trained only briefly and reaches lower SPL (34.8)
Evaluated only on PointGoal in Matterport3D with vanilla PPO; no comparison with DD-PPO or hierarchical/planner-based methods, and success-rate gains are small
